rendered: Energy density: the review's summary says that since the commercial debut of LIBs in 1991[1], energy density has risen from 150 to 250[2] Wh kg (gravimetric, per kilogram of battery). Battery cost: the review says it has steadily decreased from over $1000[3] kWh in 2008[4] to around $130[5] kWh in 2020[6], as shown in Fig. 11[7], which plots pack-level energy density and cost from 2008[8] to 2020[9]. So the starting points are 1991[10] for energy density and 2008[11] for cost, with 2020[12] as the end point for both. The review's text gives the end-point cost as around $130 kWh, while the figure's own label for the end-point pack reads $126 kWh.
